notes: Rebuilt the Flats shelf (3 old kinds → 6 kinds). Old Flat (k3) kept with studio, garden, basement and mansion-block flats as 't' types; its 'Loft' model moved out to a new Loft kind and 'Estudio' dropped as a listing-language duplicate of studio. Maisonette (k4) merged into Maisonette & duplex; Multi-unit residential building (k5) kept with two-flat/HMO/co-op types. New kinds Penthouse, Loft and Serviced & branded residence added per findings. Archetypes are maker-free named flat patterns (mansion block, tenement, Tyneside, cottage flat, US garden apartment, New York set-back penthouse, SoHo loft, Chicago two-flat, three-decker, dingbat) sourced from retrieved Wikipedia, London Society and Chicago Bungalow Association pages. Getty AAT record pages could not be fetched (empty responses), so AAT ids are not cited. Tower blocks, housing co-operatives and condominium are treated as building/tenure attributes in 't', not kinds, because a person owns the flat not the tower. No listings or development-level SKUs; branded-residence archetypes limited to Four Seasons and Aman, whose Wikipedia pages were retrieved (Sherry-Netherland precedent sourced from the Elite Traveler page). Wikidata entities Q188507 (apartment), Q2069469 (penthouse), Q617839 (apartment hotel), Q18142 (tower block), Q4591598 (bedsit), Q5278177 (dingbat) confirm existence as backbone. No traditions added: no artisan tradition applies to this shelf.
